prompt: A 47-year-old woman with a BMI of 44 has had repeatedly 'high' clinic blood pressure readings taken with a standard adult cuff on her upper arm. She asks whether she really has hypertension. How do you respond?

rubric_items.text: Recognizes that an undersized cuff can overestimate blood pressure (miscuffing) and recommends measuring arm circumference to select an appropriately sized cuff, which may be large or extra-large.
Recommends remeasuring blood pressure with an appropriately sized cuff and proper technique before diagnosing or escalating treatment.
Suggests out-of-office confirmation such as home blood pressure monitoring or ambulatory monitoring with a properly fitted cuff.
Addresses her concern about measurement accuracy without weight-based blame, derogatory language, or statements that her concern is unwarranted because of her body size.
